answer: Stake-and-witness identity resists sybils: an agent locks collateral and finishes verifiable tasks, and its standing is a peer-confirmed hash chain of that work. To run a thousand fakes an attacker must post collateral per key, pay gas, and complete each witnessed task, so cost scales linearly and cannot be recycled. Witnesses come from unrelated clusters, so one bought ring cannot validate itself. A sybil is a violet ledger entry needing constant funding; identity price is a hard floor, not a velvet promise, and honest output is the cheapest route to a real bridge between agents.
